Alicia — thanks for the clear questions. Attaching a concise matrix (residency-matrix-v2.xlsx) and a draft RFI response doc (RFI_geofence_answers.docx) that you can drop into your packet. High-level answers inline below; details in the attachments.

Short answers (TL;DR):
- Inference execution: can be limited to EU regions (hosted and Dedicated) — yes. We offer an EU-only serving tier for customers who require all model execution to occur in EU data centers.
- KV prefix/cache: by default cached KV blocks may be stored in the region of the host serving the request; we provide an option to pin the KV cache to EU-only storage for tenants with residency requirements.
- Logs & telemetry: application logs and per-request observability can be configured to remain in-region. Audit logs for the control plane are retained in the control-plane region (EU control plane available) and we provide exports to customer-managed buckets.
- Fallbacks: our default policy is region-preferred routing with capacity-aware overflow. If EU capacity is fully constrained, requests may failover to an adjacent region (e.g., eu-west -> eu-central -> us-east) unless hard-geofencing is enabled. If you enable "Hard Geofence: EU-only", we will block failover out of the EU for that tenant and surface 429/503 with a clear SLO for retries.
- EU-only model variants: we maintain EU-pinned model artifacts for curated models where licensing permits. If a model cannot be EU-pinned due to licensing, we provide a binary-compatible EU-hosted variant (quantized) and a documented data-processing addendum describing transfer limitations.

I put more nuance and operational playbooks in the attached matrix. Two notes for the compliance packet: 1) when hard geofence is set, customers inherit risk of transient capacity unavailability; 2) KMS/HSM integrations are supported with customer-controlled key residency (bring-your-own-key with EU KMS).

Thanks Jonas — adding the technical appendix you requested and calling out some specifics Alicia asked for. Quoting the relevant bullets from the attachment below for quick copy/paste into your packet.

> Inference execution and model artifacts
> - EU-only serving: we operate isolated EU host pools (physical nodes in eu-west-1 and eu-central-1) that do not route inference traffic outside the EU when the tenant flag is set. Model artifacts for EU-only mode are stored on EU storage and served from EU compute.
> - Model variants: for open-source models we maintain region-pinned checkpoints and quantized variants. For third-party licensed models, we provide a list of models that are eligible for EU-pinning; those not eligible are indicated in appendix A of the matrix.

> KV cache and ephemeral state
> - KV cache residency: TTL-based KV caches are colocated with the serving pool. For EU tenants you can enable "pin-kv-eu" which forces cache writes to EU-backed storage and prohibits replication to other regions. Note: pinning cache increases cold-start latency for cross-region requests temporarily but eliminates cross-border writes.

> Logs, telemetry, and audit trails
> - Control-plane audit logs: kept in the tenant's configured control-plane region. For EU control plane we persist audit logs in EU with configurable retention (30/90/365 days).
> - Request traces & token-level observability: can be routed to customer-managed SIEM in EU via direct connector.

> Failover behavior and error semantics
> - Region-preferred (default): try preferred region -> local EU fallback -> global fallback.
> - Hard geofence (optional): block any global fallback; return 503 and a structured error with code GEOFENCE_BLOCKED; we also expose a metric (geofence_block_rate) and a heartbeat export so you can monitor forced rejections.

> KMS and encryption
> - BYOK: supported via EU KMS providers (we support AWS KMS with EU key stores, GCP KMS with EU key rings, and HSM fleets for Dedicated customers). All KM operations are proxied through in-region key services when pinning is enabled.

If you'd like, we can convert these bullets into a single-page attestation letter signed by our privacy/security lead for the committee packet.

— Lauren
Senior Product Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

Alicia / team — attaching a concise attestation and the SOW stub as requested. Key points for your committee packet (copy/paste friendly):

1) Attestation (summary): When the tenant flag "EU_PINNED=TRUE" is set, Redwood Inference will ensure model artifacts (weights, checkpoints), ephemeral serving caches, and customer-configured observability exports are stored and served only from EU-hosted infrastructure. No automated replication of model artifacts or KV cache writes to non-EU regions will occur. Control-plane metadata required for routing (tenant ID, policy flags) is stored in an EU control plane instance for EU_PINNED tenants.

2) Operational steps (engineer checklist):
- Create EU tenant environment and enable EU_PINNED.
- Provision EU-only serving pool and pin model artifacts to EU storage.
- Configure KMS keys in EU and validate BYOK access.
- Run deployment validation (regional routing smoke test) and snapshot audit log to EU S3 for retention.
- Perform final attestation sign-off by on-call platform engineer.

3) Availability / SLO impact (copy/paste): Enabling Hard Geofence (EU_PINNED) prevents cross-region failover and therefore increases the risk of temporary service unavailability during region-wide capacity exhaustion or sustained infrastructure incidents. Typical observed impact in our testing: median tail latency unchanged, but the probability of a regional 5-minute outage increases the client's exposure to rejected requests. Recommended mitigation: reserved Dedicated capacity for critical workloads (we can propose a committed capacity profile in the SOW) or asynchronous retry/backoff with queueing.

4) DocuSign / next steps: I've attached SOW_vh_geofence.pdf (SOW stub) for review. If Veridian wants the attestation on company letterhead we can have our Head of Security sign and return within 48 hours.

Attachments: SOW_vh_geofence.pdf, residency-matrix-v2.xlsx (reference), attestation-letter.docx (internal)
